batchId: Claude manual-research batch dc-missing (10 identities that had no profile)
method: Facts taken from fetched pages (mostly Wikipedia and Tolkien Gateway, plus search-result articles); claims a page did not support were left out. No numeric tiers. All records provisional until a different contributor checks them.

characters.continuity: Dark Multiverse Batman from Dark Nights: Metal (2017) and its tie-in one-shot. Not the mainline Bruce Wayne.
characters.summary: Bruce Wayne of Earth -32, chosen by a Green Lantern ring as a child after his parents' murder. His rage and will corrupted the ring into a lethal weapon.

techniques: Power ring pushed past normal limits by his will, with the no-killing restriction overridden
Dark constructs described as stronger than his world's whole Green Lantern Corps
Murdered every Green Lantern and Guardian in his universe
Beat Hal Jordan and laid waste to Coast City

weaknesses: Raven nearly beat him by seizing control of his constructs
Defeated with the other Dark Knights by the Justice League

sources.supports: Dawnbreaker: ring chose young Bruce of Earth -32; will overrode the no-kill limit; dark constructs; killed his Corps; fought Hal Jordan; nearly beaten by Raven.
Dawnbreaker origin: young Bruce chosen by a power ring, corrupts it with rage and murders every Green Lantern and Oan in his universe.
Seven evil Batmen from the Dark Multiverse serve Barbatos; the Justice League defeats the Dark Knights.

unknowns: New profile 2026-11-15 (Claude): built only from the cited pages; anything they did not state was left out. Not independently reviewed.

characters.formDifferences: A Green Lantern ring wielder rather than an unpowered detective: ring constructs and flight replace gadgets, and he kills freely.

characters.continuity: Post-Crisis DC Comics: Emerald Twilight (1994), Zero Hour and The Final Night.
characters.summary: Hal Jordan after Coast City's destruction: he seized the Central Power Battery, took the name Parallax and tried to rewrite history. Later stories attribute this to a fear parasite.

techniques: Solid-light constructs and energy on a far greater scale after absorbing the Central Power Battery
Reality alteration and time manipulation
Destroyed the Green Lantern Corps, killing Kilowog and Sinestro
Reignited the Sun in The Final Night

weaknesses: Exhausted most of his power in Zero Hour and was shot by Green Arrow
Fearless opponents resist Parallax
Gave his life reigniting the Sun

sources.supports: Parallax: Hal Jordan destroys the Corps, tries to rewrite history in Zero Hour, sacrifices himself in Final Night; powers include constructs, reality and time alteration.
Hal attacked Oa, took the Central Power Battery, killed Kilowog and Sinestro, was shot by Green Arrow in Zero Hour and died in Final Night.

characters.id: dc:Green Lantern (Hal Jordan)|White Lantern Hal Jordan
characters.summary: Hal Jordan bonded with the Entity, the embodiment of life itself, at the climax of Blackest Night. In this form he wields the white light of creation, capable of life-manipulation and overcoming necrotic forces.

techniques: White light energy constructs
Life-restoration waves
Creation-based constructs
White light constructs fuelled by life
Created further white rings and made other heroes White Lanterns
Restored Black Hand to life, which led to Nekron's destruction

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Temporary state tied directly to the Entity's presence
Vulnerability to corruption if willpower wavers
Temporary: held only during the final battle with Nekron
White rings reject wearers they judge unsuitable
limitations: The White Lantern state is temporary and dependent on the Entity's will
characters.formDifferences: Replaces standard green ring powers with the unified life spectrum of the White Lantern Corps, granting creation and resurrection abilities.

sources.supports: Hal Jordan becoming the White Lantern and defeating Nekron
White Lanterns use life-fuelled white constructs; Hal Jordan made extra rings and revived Nekron's victims.

feats.claim: Resurrected Black Hand and severed Nekron's connection to the living universe.

notableResults.note: Used the Entity to push back the embodiment of death

conditional.ability: Life creation, resurrection, and ultimate white light manipulation
conditional.dependsOn: Bonding with the Entity of Life

campaignTags.claim: Flies freely using the power of the White Lantern ring and Entity
Restores life and heals fatal injuries using the white light of creation
Resurrects and heals fallen heroes and entities during Blackest Night

unknowns: Full potential of White Lantern ring without the direct presence of the Entity.

characters.summary: Superman after killing Doomsday and inhaling its toxic remains. The infection transformed him into a grey-skinned, monstrous hybrid known as Superdoom, combining his Kryptonian powers with Doomsday's virulent rage and physical adaptation.

techniques: Doomsday-virus energy breath
Brute-force shockwave punches
Adaptive physical evolution
Doomsday-like strength on top of his own powers
The infection incinerates anything within about 100 yards
Tore off Cyborg Superman's arm and stopped Brainiac

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Mental corruption and loss of control to the 'Superdoom' persona
Vulnerability to magical attacks and specialized psychic probes
Superdoom takes over and attacks allies, including Wonder Woman
Cured only when the infection was purged
limitations: Constant mental battle against the invasive Doomsday persona
characters.formDifferences: Changes Superman's appearance to a grey, rocky monster and enhances physical strength and aggression while threatening his moral restraint.

sources.supports: Superman's infection by Doomsday and transformation into Superdoom

characters.continuity: DC One Million (1998) and DC Comics lore

techniques: Reality reconstruction
Universe creation
Golden solar energy projection
With the future Hourman, recreated Lois Lane and then Krypton and its people

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Solaris tried to kill him by firing kryptonite into the Sun

depictions.title: DC One Million (1998): the original Superman in the 853rd century.

sources.supports: Superman Prime One Million's origin, 15,000 years in the sun, and reality-warping powers
DC One Million's Superman dynasty: successors down to Kal Kent, who leads Justice Legion A in the 853rd century.
